title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 3.73 (versions follow prime numbers; 373 after 367): Luma eats what is new on the disks, reads it where it is and says she ate it. The kernel kept the host's folders watched only for a process asleep on a greeting; now also for one asleep on its screen, and wakes it when a new file is quiet. She looks at the file where it is (a zero byte: not text) and puts on her shelf a disk book holding only its content print and its address; nothing is copied, her reader reads it in its place (request 37, read only), and a file no longer there is passed over. Same print again: she knew it, nothing is done. When she eats something she says so in her talk ("me comí ..."). Her shelf list grows to her house (it had a fixed 4096-byte room). Tested in a copy: reading a book in place gives exactly the same words and final print as reading it copied; a changed poem greeted 68 s after saving (the kernel's quiet rule); a binary was not eaten; idle CPU unchanged. Kernel host-watch, greeting, screen and family tests: 96 passing, 3 failing, identical with and without the change; the full suite was not run. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v3.73: Luma come lo nuevo de los discos. Prototipo de investigación.
